subject: Information Theory
title: Transparency and Open Data
description: A short lesson to help you apply Transparency and Open Data.

hook.text: When New York published hospital infection rates in 2007, rates dropped 45% in two years. Transparency changed behavior.

buildup.text: Open data makes government info publicly accessible: budgets, contracts, environmental data, and performance metrics.

discovery.text: Transparency raises mutual information between government actions and public knowledge—cutting corruption incentives.

twist.text: Raw data without context can mislead. Publishing numbers without analysis creates the illusion of transparency.

climax.text: Effective transparency requires data release and civic capacity to interpret it. Information needs informed receivers.

punchline.text: Publish the data. Watch behavior change. Transparency is pressure.

quiz.question: Why isn't publishing raw data alone sufficient for transparency?
options: Data without context or analysis can mislead rather than inform
